column1: # Bare surnames the English text uses on their own, tied to the full-name glossary entry
# whose forms supply them (last word of each locale's full form). Left out on purpose:
# surnames that also name a facility, vehicle or eponymous term (Glenn → Glenn Research
# Center, Shepard → New Shepard, Goddard → Goddard Space Flight Center, Oberth → Oberth
# effect, Drake → Drake equation, Kuiper → Kuiper Belt, Rubin → Rubin Observatory) and
# common words (Cooper, Carpenter, Scott, Duke, Bean, Young, White).
# surname \t full-name key [\t only in paths matching this regex]
# Added for the hi pass: in non-Latin text a Latin "Stafford" or "Bean" can only be the
# person, and a Latin-script locale keeps the surname as it is (the form equals the key).
# Shepard is guarded against "New Shepard" in glossary-apply.mjs.
